title: Content Browser SDK
markdown:
For AI agents: the docs index is at https://developer.orangelogic.com/llms.txt. Append .md to any documentation page URL to get its markdown version.

Orange Logic’s content browser allows authenticated users to browse Orange Logic assets in external web applications. You can use the Content Browser SDK to develop custom integrations between your Orange Logic platform and other applications.

For example, let’s say your organization’s creative team stores images in Orange Logic. However, the marketing team uses a Content Management System (CMS) to build webpages. You can add the content browser to your CMS so users can search, filter, and select assets directly from Orange Logic, and then use them in your CMS.

![Sample content browser (v2.1.0)](https://files.readme.io/8bd467223a9b030cb815e1e9902cd6646dfbbce9e5a661f4be15f17c2e99c162-content_browser_display_config_example.png)

Sample content browser (v2.1.0)

With Orange Logic’s content browser, users can find assets with any file extension, apply transformations, add tracking parameters to URLs, preview videos, and more. To learn how to use the content browser interface, watch the following video, which shows content browser version 2.1.0 with tracking parameters and transformations activated.

> ### **Note**   [Skip link to ,[object Object]](https://developer.orangelogic.com/docs/content-browser-sdk\#note)

## User access to assets   [Skip link to User access to assets](https://developer.orangelogic.com/docs/content-browser-sdk\#user-access-to-assets)

Orange Logic only returns the assets that users have the [Permissions and Security Functions](https://developer.orangelogic.com/reference/security-functions-for-the-content-browser-sdk) to access. Additionally, when you configure the content browser, you can limit:

- The available [Asset Types](https://developer.orangelogic.com/reference/assets#asset-type-and-subtype). For example, you could limit the content browser to display only videos and images.
- The available Visibility Classes. For example, you could show only assets with the “Public” Visibility Class.
- The Asset Types and Subtypes that display image representatives. For example, you could allow representatives for all Asset Subtypes except for the “Legal documents” subtype.

### Supported file extensions and asset previews   [Skip link to Supported file extensions and asset previews](https://developer.orangelogic.com/docs/content-browser-sdk\#supported-file-extensions-and-asset-previews)

All file extensions are supported.

- Video previews include video scrubbing and playback.
- Audio previews are limited to an audio wave representative image. Audio playback is not supported yet.
- When users select assets of the “Other” asset type, such as PDFs and PPTX files, they can only preview and access the asset representative, not the complete asset.

## Content Browser SDK examples   [Skip link to Content Browser SDK examples](https://developer.orangelogic.com/docs/content-browser-sdk\#content-browser-sdk-examples)

The content browser is extremely flexible. Use these examples as inspiration.

### Orange Logic’s demo page   [Skip link to Orange Logic’s demo page](https://developer.orangelogic.com/docs/content-browser-sdk\#orange-logics-demo-page)

You can try the Content Browser SDK for yourself. Go to our [demo page](https://downloads.orangelogic.com/ContentBrowserSDK/v2.2.0/CBSDKdemo.html).

1. Click “Load config” to load the browser.

2. Log in to your organization’s Orange Logic environment.

3. Adjust the instance-specific [configurations](https://developer.orangelogic.com/reference/configure-the-content-browser#customize-individual-content-browsers) in the “Config” box to see how the browser interface changes.
![Content Browser SDK demo](https://files.readme.io/2eeb54b7c5dc45e107e92c95591d96d570d19b641064f69ac8077745707d0e4c-Content_browser_demo.png)

Content Browser SDK demo


For example, by default file size and tags do not appear on the previews of assets in the content browser.

However, you can update the `displayInfo` attribute from its default:

```undefined
"displayInfo": {
"title": true,
"dimension": true,
"fileSize": false,
"tags": false
}
```

to:

```undefined
"displayInfo": {
"title": true,
"dimension": true,
"fileSize": true,
"tags": true
}
```

So that file size and tags appear on the preview of each asset:

![Content browser demo configured to include file size and tags in each asset’s preview.](https://files.readme.io/9917b2ab90dbc073aef5591f84023183487408d6aa23c1a609fcc90bb3f1d693-content_browser_display_config_example.png)

Content browser demo configured to include file size and tags in each asset’s preview.

### JavaScript example   [Skip link to JavaScript example](https://developer.orangelogic.com/docs/content-browser-sdk\#javascript-example)

In [this JavaScript example](https://cortex-gab-sandbox.w3spaces.com/), the `extraField` attribute is specified as `["CoreField.alternative-description"]` and `onImageSelected` is specified as:

JavaScript

```javascript
function (assets) {
          console.log(assets);
          document.getElementById("myImage").src=assets[0].imageUrl;
          document.getElementById("myImage").alt=assets[0].extraFields['CoreField.alternative-description'];
        }
```

Therefore, the selected image’s alternative description is displayed when a user hovers over it.

### React example   [Skip link to React example](https://developer.orangelogic.com/docs/content-browser-sdk\#react-example)

Sanity.io is a CMS that stores and pushes content to digital platforms. [Orange Logic’s Sanity.io integration](https://www.sanity.io/plugins/orangedam-asset-browser) retrieves images from Orange Logic and adds them to Sanity. It’s a great example of using Orange Logic’s content browser in an integration.

> ℹ️
>
> ### **Note**   [Skip link to ,[object Object]](https://developer.orangelogic.com/docs/content-browser-sdk\#note-1)
>
> The Sanity.io example uses version 1 of the content browser SDK.
